SL-000013.transcript:
Member (Fatima Morrison): My dental claim was declined, and the same kind of claim was paid in the spring.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Hi Fatima Morrison, Harpreet Gill here — let me pull that up.
Member (Fatima Morrison): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Fatima Morrison): Yes, that's right.
Member (Fatima Morrison): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Fatima Morrison): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Fatima Morrison): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Fatima Morrison): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Fatima Morrison): They said they billed it the same way as always.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with the earlier paid claims on the file and the plan booklet.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Fatima Morrison): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Member (Fatima Morrison): So is this actually getting fixed today?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Fatima Morrison): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Fatima Morrison): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Fatima Morrison): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.
SL-000013.narrative_summary: Fatima Morrison, a Sun Life member, contacted support on a declined claim case. Agent Harpreet Gill compared this claim with the earlier paid claims on the file and the plan booklet. In the end, it was not resolved on this interaction, and the member rated it CSAT 3 (neutral).

SL-000044.transcript:
Member (Chantal Martin): I asked to transfer my pension from my old employer's plan to my bank and it still hasn't moved.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Hi Chantal Martin, Sophie Belanger here — let me pull that up.
Member (Chantal Martin): The receiving institution says they never got anything.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Chantal Martin): Yes, that's right.
Member (Chantal Martin): The market's moved since then and I've lost money waiting.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Where is the money going?
Member (Chantal Martin): To an RRSP at my bank. They say they're waiting on Sun Life.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): When did you send in the transfer request?
Member (Chantal Martin): In June. I signed everything they sent me.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Did the bank send you a transfer form to sign as well?
Member (Chantal Martin): I think so. They handled their side.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Let me take a look. I've traced the transfer request and the paperwork on the plan account.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Your request came in on June 14. The transfer is waiting on the signed transfer authorization from the receiving institution, which is standard for locked-in pension money.
Member (Chantal Martin): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): The transfer is waiting on the signed transfer form from the receiving institution. I can't release it until that arrives, but I've sent them a reminder.
Member (Chantal Martin): So I've lost money because of a form nobody told me about?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): I understand. I've noted on your file that you've been waiting since June, so it's visible if this needs a review.
Member (Chantal Martin): Who follows up?
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Retirement services will. I've asked them to call you once the form arrives.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): To recap, everything's noted on your file, and the team will follow up with you.
Member (Chantal Martin): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Sophie Belanger): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Hannah O'Brien): My life insurance premium tripled and nobody warned me.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Hi Hannah O'Brien, Jasmine Wong here — let me pull that up.

Agent (Jasmine Wong): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.

Member (Mathieu Lavoie): I'm waiting on a decision on my disability claim and nobody has called me.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Hi Mathieu Lavoie, Priya Sandhu here — let me pull that up.
Member (Mathieu Lavoie): I don't know who my case manager is.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?

Member (Mathieu Lavoie): My employer says they sent their part weeks ago.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): When did you go off work?
Member (Mathieu Lavoie): Six weeks ago. I submitted my part in the first week.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Have you been contacted by a case manager yet?
Member (Mathieu Lavoie): Not that I know of. Nobody has called me.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Is there a good number and time to reach you?
Member (Mathieu Lavoie): My mobile, any time before three. I have appointments in the afternoons.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Are you receiving any other income right now, like sick days from work?
Member (Mathieu Lavoie): My sick days ran out two weeks ago.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the disability file and the case manager's task list.

Agent (Priya Sandhu): Your file has your statement and your doctor's statement. I'm checking whether the employer's statement has come in.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Once the file is complete, the case manager makes the decision and calls you to explain it.
Member (Mathieu Lavoie): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): The file is still waiting on the employer's statement. I've flagged it to your case manager, but I can't make a decision on the claim from here.
Member (Mathieu Lavoie): So I'm still waiting with no income?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I know that's hard. I've marked the file as a priority because you have no other income right now.
Member (Mathieu Lavoie): Is there anything I can do to speed it up?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Ask HR for the date they sent the statement. If it's missing, that's the one thing holding the file.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): To recap: the file is waiting on the employer's statement, your case manager has been asked to call you, and I've noted your preferred contact times.
Member (Mathieu Lavoie): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Arjun Patel): My dentist's crown request under the Canadian Dental Care Plan was denied, and the letter doesn't say why.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Hi Arjun Patel, Harpreet Gill here — let me pull that up.
Member (Arjun Patel): The letter only says it doesn't meet plan criteria.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Can you confirm your CDCP member ID and date of birth?
Member (Arjun Patel): The member ID is on the welcome letter.

Agent (Harpreet Gill): I'm looking at the latest assessment on your file now.
Member (Arjun Patel): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): The decision follows the plan criteria set by Health Canada, and I don't have a more specific reason on my screen. Your dentist can submit a new request with more clinical notes, and I've noted that you asked for the reason.
Member (Arjun Patel): So nobody can tell me why?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I know that's frustrating. I've asked for the specific criterion to be sent to you and your dentist in writing.
Member (Arjun Patel): What should my dentist include this time?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): A description of the crack, any symptoms, and a dated X-ray. Those are the most common gaps on crown requests.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): To recap, everything's noted on your file, and the team will follow up with you.
Member (Arjun Patel): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Arjun Martin): My dentist's claim came back declined and nobody's explained why.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Hi Arjun Martin, Ryan MacDonald here — let me pull that up.
Member (Arjun Martin): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Arjun Martin): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Arjun Martin): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Arjun Martin): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Arjun Martin): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Arjun Martin): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Arjun Martin): They said they billed it the same way as always.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with the earlier paid claims on the file and the plan booklet.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Okay, I've got it pulled up now.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Arjun Martin): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Member (Arjun Martin): So is this actually getting fixed today?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Arjun Martin): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Arjun Martin): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Arjun Martin): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

Member (Noah Ahmed): My dental claim was declined, and the same kind of claim was paid in the spring.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Hi Noah Ahmed, Ryan MacDonald here — let me pull that up.
Member (Noah Ahmed): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Noah Ahmed): Yes, that's right.
Member (Noah Ahmed): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Noah Ahmed): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Noah Ahmed): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Noah Ahmed): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Noah Ahmed): They said they billed it the same way as always.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with the earlier paid claims on the file and the plan booklet.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Noah Ahmed): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Member (Noah Ahmed): So is this actually getting fixed today?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Noah Ahmed): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Noah Ahmed): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Noah Ahmed): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Ryan MacDonald): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

Member (Mei Fortin): I asked to transfer my pension from my old employer's plan to my bank and it still hasn't moved.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Hi Mei Fortin, Aisha Rahman here — let me pull that up.
Member (Mei Fortin): The receiving institution says they never got anything.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?

Member (Mei Fortin): The market's moved since then and I've lost money waiting.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Which plan is the transfer from?

Agent (Aisha Rahman): Where is the money going?
Member (Mei Fortin): To an RRSP at my bank. They say they're waiting on Sun Life.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): When did you send in the transfer request?
Member (Mei Fortin): In June. I signed everything they sent me.

Agent (Aisha Rahman): Until that form arrives, the funds stay invested in your current options, so they've moved with the market.

Agent (Aisha Rahman): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): The transfer was held because the receiving institution's form wasn't signed. It came in this morning, so I've released it, and the funds will move within five business days.
Member (Mei Fortin): So it's finally moving?
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Yes. The form arrived this morning, and I've released the transfer.
Member (Mei Fortin): How long until my bank has it?
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Usually five business days, and you'll get a confirmation letter from us.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): So the transfer is released and should reach your bank within five business days.
Member (Mei Fortin): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

SL-001292.transcript:
Member (Gurpreet Kim): My son needs braces and I want to know what my plan pays before we commit.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Hi Gurpreet Kim, Chloe Gagnon here — let me pull that up.
Member (Gurpreet Kim): The orthodontist wants to start next month.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Happy to check that for you.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Gurpreet Kim): Yes, that's right.
Member (Gurpreet Kim): My spouse has coverage through her work too.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Is he listed as a dependant on your plan?
Member (Gurpreet Kim): Yes, since he was born.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): How old is he?
Member (Gurpreet Kim): Fourteen.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Do you have a treatment plan or cost estimate from the orthodontist?
Member (Gurpreet Kim): They gave me an estimate of about six thousand dollars.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Let me take a look. I've checked the plan booklet and dependant coverage on the certificate.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Orthodontic coverage depends on your employer's plan, so I'm checking your certificate now.
Member (Gurpreet Kim): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Orthodontics is covered at 50% up to a 2,500-dollar lifetime maximum for dependants under 19. I recommend a pre-determination first, and I've emailed you the steps.
Member (Gurpreet Kim): What's a pre-determination?
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): The orthodontist sends the treatment plan first, and we confirm exactly what's covered before any work starts.
Member (Gurpreet Kim): Great, that helps.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): I'll also send the coordination-of-benefits form for your spouse's plan.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): So, 50% up to 2,500 dollars, a pre-determination first, and your spouse's plan can cover part of the rest.
Member (Gurpreet Kim): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

SL-001304.transcript:
Member (Owen Kim): My dental claim was declined, and the same kind of claim was paid in the spring.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Hi Owen Kim, Jasmine Wong here — let me pull that up.
Member (Owen Kim): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Owen Kim): Yes, that's right.
Member (Owen Kim): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Owen Kim): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Has this type of claim been paid before?
Member (Owen Kim): Yes, in the spring. Same dentist, same kind of work, and it went through with no problem.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Owen Kim): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Owen Kim): They said they billed it the same way as always.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with the earlier paid claims on the file and the plan booklet.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Owen Kim): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): The decline is correct under your employer's plan, because this service has an annual maximum and it's been reached. I can send you the plan wording, and your plan administrator at work can confirm the limits.
Member (Owen Kim): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Owen Kim): Can I appeal it?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): You can ask for a review. I've opened one and noted that you weren't told about the separate maximum.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Owen Kim): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

SL-001499.transcript:
Member (Noah O'Brien): My dentist's crown request under the Canadian Dental Care Plan was denied, and the letter doesn't say why.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Hi Noah O'Brien, Marc Tremblay here — let me pull that up.
Member (Noah O'Brien): My dentist sent the X-rays twice.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Can you confirm your CDCP member ID and date of birth?
Member (Noah O'Brien): The member ID is on the welcome letter.
Member (Noah O'Brien): The letter only says it doesn't meet plan criteria.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Which procedure was the request for?
Member (Noah O'Brien): A crown on a back tooth. My dentist says it's cracked.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Is this the first request or a resubmission?
Member (Noah O'Brien): The second. The first was denied in July.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Are you in any pain right now?
Member (Noah O'Brien): Some. It's manageable, but I can't chew on that side.

Member (Noah O'Brien): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Member (Noah O'Brien): So is this actually getting fixed today?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): The decision follows the plan criteria set by Health Canada, and I don't have a more specific reason on my screen. Your dentist can submit a new request with more clinical notes, and I've noted that you asked for the reason.
Member (Noah O'Brien): So nobody can tell me why?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): I know that's frustrating. I've asked for the specific criterion to be sent to you and your dentist in writing.
Member (Noah O'Brien): What should my dentist include this time?
Agent (Marc Tremblay): A description of the crack, any symptoms, and a dated X-ray. Those are the most common gaps on crown requests.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): To recap: the denial stands for now, I've recorded your request for the specific reason, and your dentist can resubmit with more clinical notes.
Member (Noah O'Brien): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Marc Tremblay): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

Member (Liam Singh): My dental claim was declined, and the same kind of claim was paid in the spring.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Hi Liam Singh, Kevin Nguyen here — let me pull that up.
Member (Liam Singh): It only shows a code on the explanation of benefits.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Liam Singh): Yes, that's right.
Member (Liam Singh): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Liam Singh): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Liam Singh): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?
Member (Liam Singh): No, same job, same plan. My daughter was added last year but that's it.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Did the dental office say anything about how they billed it?
Member (Liam Singh): They said they billed it the same way as always.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Let me take a look. I've compared this claim with the earlier paid claims on the file and the plan booklet.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): I've compared this claim with the one from the spring. The earlier filling was billed under a basic services code, and this one came in under a major restorative code.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Under your plan, major restorative work has a separate annual maximum, and that's where the decline came from.
Member (Liam Singh): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): The earlier claims went through under a different benefit code. I've resubmitted this one under the right code, and it should be paid at 80% within five business days.
Member (Liam Singh): So it was just the wrong code?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): That's what it looks like. I've resubmitted it under the basic services code, which matches what was done.
Member (Liam Singh): Do I need to tell my dentist?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): No need. I've added a note, and the payment will come to you since the claim was already paid at the office.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): To recap, everything's noted on your file, and the team will follow up with you.
Member (Liam Singh): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Gurpreet Wilson): My Canadian Dental Care Plan crown request was denied and even the supervisor couldn't tell me why.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Hi Gurpreet Wilson, Aisha Rahman here — let me pull that up.
Member (Gurpreet Wilson): The letter only says it doesn't meet plan criteria.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): I hear you, and I want to get this sorted out rather than just tell you what the policy says.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Can you confirm your CDCP member ID and date of birth?
Member (Gurpreet Wilson): The member ID is on the welcome letter.
Member (Gurpreet Wilson): My dentist sent the X-rays twice.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Is this the first request or a resubmission?
Member (Gurpreet Wilson): The second. The first was denied in July.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Did the letter mention any documents that were missing?
Member (Gurpreet Wilson): No, just that it doesn't meet the criteria.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Has the dental office called us about this directly?
Member (Gurpreet Wilson): They said they called and got the same answer as me.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Let me take a look. I've reviewed the pre-authorization request and the documents received from the dental office.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): The assessment is done against the plan's criteria for crowns, which are set by Health Canada.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): I'm looking at the latest assessment on your file now.
Member (Gurpreet Wilson): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): The decision follows the plan criteria set by Health Canada, and I don't have a more specific reason on my screen. Your dentist can submit a new request with more clinical notes, and I've noted that you asked for the reason.
Member (Gurpreet Wilson): So nobody can tell me why?
Agent (Aisha Rahman): I know that's frustrating. I've asked for the specific criterion to be sent to you and your dentist in writing.
Member (Gurpreet Wilson): What should my dentist include this time?
Agent (Aisha Rahman): A description of the crack, any symptoms, and a dated X-ray. Those are the most common gaps on crown requests.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): To recap: the denial stands for now, I've recorded your request for the specific reason, and your dentist can resubmit with more clinical notes.
Member (Gurpreet Wilson): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Aisha Rahman): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

SL-001755.transcript:
Member (Gurpreet Fortin): My son needs braces and I want to know what my plan pays before we commit.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Hi Gurpreet Fortin, Priya Sandhu here — let me pull that up.
Member (Gurpreet Fortin): The orthodontist wants to start next month.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Happy to check that for you.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Gurpreet Fortin): Yes, that's right.
Member (Gurpreet Fortin): My spouse has coverage through her work too.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Is he listed as a dependant on your plan?
Member (Gurpreet Fortin): Yes, since he was born.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): How old is he?
Member (Gurpreet Fortin): Fourteen.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Do you have a treatment plan or cost estimate from the orthodontist?
Member (Gurpreet Fortin): They gave me an estimate of about six thousand dollars.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Has he had any orthodontic work covered before?
Member (Gurpreet Fortin): No, this is the first time.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Let me take a look. I've checked the plan booklet and dependant coverage on the certificate.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Orthodontic coverage depends on your employer's plan, so I'm checking your certificate now.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): If your spouse has coverage too, their plan can pick up part of what's left after ours pays.
Member (Gurpreet Fortin): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Orthodontics isn't part of your employer's plan. I can send you the booklet section, and your plan administrator at work can confirm whether that's changing.
Member (Gurpreet Fortin): That's disappointing.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): I understand. Some employers offer a health spending account that can be used for orthodontics.
Member (Gurpreet Fortin): How would I check that?
Agent (Priya Sandhu): It would show under Accounts in the app. I don't see one on your certificate, but HR can confirm.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): To recap: orthodontics isn't in your employer's plan right now, and HR can tell you if that's changing.
Member (Gurpreet Fortin): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Priya Sandhu): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Arjun Roy): I'm waiting on a decision on my disability claim and nobody has called me.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Hi Arjun Roy, Kevin Nguyen here — let me pull that up.
Member (Arjun Roy): My employer says they sent their part weeks ago.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): I completely understand how frustrating that is — let me see what's actually happening on our end.

Member (Arjun Roy): Yes, that's right.
Member (Arjun Roy): I don't know who my case manager is.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): When did you go off work?

Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Have you been contacted by a case manager yet?

Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.

Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Once the file is complete, the case manager makes the decision and calls you to explain it.
Member (Arjun Roy): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Your claim was approved yesterday. The first payment goes out Friday, and your case manager will call you this week to talk about your return-to-work plan.
Member (Arjun Roy): So when does the first payment come?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): It's scheduled for Friday, and it includes the weeks since your waiting period ended.
Member (Arjun Roy): Who do I contact if something changes?
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Your case manager is Denise. I've sent you her direct line by secure message.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): To recap: your claim is approved, the first payment is Friday, and Denise will call this week about your return-to-work plan.
Member (Arjun Roy): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Kevin Nguyen): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Olivia Ahmed): My dentist's crown request under the Canadian Dental Care Plan was denied, and the letter doesn't say why.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Hi Olivia Ahmed, Harpreet Gill here — let me pull that up.
Member (Olivia Ahmed): The letter only says it doesn't meet plan criteria.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): That's really not what should happen — give me a second to look into it properly.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Can you confirm your CDCP member ID and date of birth?
Member (Olivia Ahmed): The member ID is on the welcome letter.
Member (Olivia Ahmed): My dentist sent the X-rays twice.

Member (Olivia Ahmed): A crown on a back tooth. My dentist says it's cracked.

Member (Olivia Ahmed): No, just that it doesn't meet the criteria.

Agent (Harpreet Gill): Thanks for holding — I've got the full picture now.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): The assessment is done against the plan's criteria for crowns, which are set by Health Canada.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): I'm looking at the latest assessment on your file now.
Member (Olivia Ahmed): Okay. What's the actual next step here?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Give me one more moment while I confirm the details.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): The first request was missing the radiograph date. The second one is complete and has been assessed, and it's approved. Your dentist will get the confirmation today.
Member (Olivia Ahmed): So the crown is covered now?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Yes. It's approved at your plan's coverage level, and your dentist will get the confirmation today.
Member (Olivia Ahmed): Do I pay anything?
Agent (Harpreet Gill): That depends on your co-payment level. Your dentist will see it on the confirmation.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): To recap: the crown is approved, and your dentist will get the confirmation today with your co-payment.
Member (Olivia Ahmed): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Harpreet Gill): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Agent (Jasmine Wong): The transfer is waiting on the signed transfer form from the receiving institution. I can't release it until that arrives, but I've sent them a reminder.
Member (Lucas Chen): So I've lost money because of a form nobody told me about?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): I understand. I've noted on your file that you've been waiting since June, so it's visible if this needs a review.
Member (Lucas Chen): Who follows up?
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Retirement services will. I've asked them to call you once the form arrives.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): To recap: we're waiting on your bank's signed form, a reminder has gone to them today, and retirement services will call you when it's in.
Member (Lucas Chen): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Jasmine Wong): Thanks for bearing with me. Everything's noted on your file, and you'll hear back as I said.

Agent (Harpreet Gill): So the claim has been resubmitted under the right code, and you should see it paid at 80% within five business days.

Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Can you confirm your plan and certificate number and your date of birth so I'm in the right file?
Member (Tyler Kim): It's through my employer. The certificate number should be on my benefits card.
Member (Tyler Kim): The booklet says 80%, but the filling was paid at zero.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Which claim are you calling about, the date of service or the provider?
Member (Tyler Kim): The one from the 12th, at my dentist. It was a regular cleaning plus a filling.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Was this submitted by your provider or by you through the app?
Member (Tyler Kim): The dentist sent it directly. That's how it's always worked before.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Has anything changed with your coverage, like a new job or a new dependant?

Member (Tyler Kim): Nobody explained there was a separate maximum.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): You're right, the explanation of benefits only shows a code, and that isn't enough. I'm noting that on your file.
Member (Tyler Kim): Can I appeal it?

Agent (Chloe Gagnon): To recap: the decline stands under your plan's annual maximum, a review is open, and I've emailed you the plan wording.
Member (Tyler Kim): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Chloe Gagnon): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.

Member (Liam Martin): My dentist's crown request under the Canadian Dental Care Plan was denied, and the letter doesn't say why.
